anomalies.observed: C1 is 0.1uF/16V, while the other charge-pump and display-supply capacitors in the EPD section are 1uF/25V (C5, C7, C8, C10) or 1uF/6.3V (C2). C1 is the only one of these with a 0.1uF value.
anomalies.expected: The spec lists C1 among the 1 uF capacitors of the PDI reference circuit ("C1 (G1 group only): 1 µF/6.3 V"), and the spec's default group lists "C1/C5/C7/C8/C9/C10 = 1 µF/25 V". C1 should therefore be a 1 uF part.
anomalies.impact: The bulk decoupling on the EPD display power rail (Display_Power_Switch, which feeds the panel VDD/VDDIO and the boost converter) is about ten times smaller than intended. This can cause ripple and insufficient charge reserve during the panel's high-current refresh and boost transients.

anomalies.observed: C11 is a 0.1uF capacitor (Device:C) but uses the inductor footprint Inductor_SMD:L_0805_2012Metric_Pad1.05x1.20mm_HandSolder. Its pin 1 is on a net by itself, so the part is connected to GND only through pin 2 and does nothing.
anomalies.expected: A decoupling capacitor should use a capacitor footprint and be connected across the supply it is meant to decouple. The spec does not mention C11, so this is judged from standard practice.
anomalies.impact: A floating cap that was meant to decouple a rail may not filter that rail. If the footprint is wrong, the wrong part may be placed at assembly.

anomalies.observed: The keyboard LED anode pin U4.26 (LEDA_1_2) shares the net "GPIO" with SKW92A pin U5.46 (I2C_SD). The other keyboard LED pins (U4.23, U4.24, U4.25) go to their own LED0–LED3 nets, but the LED0 net (U5.35, P0_LED) has no keyboard pin attached.
anomalies.expected: Keyboard LED pin 26 should be on the LED0 net with the other keyboard LED pins, not on an I2C line.
anomalies.impact: The keyboard backlight LED for that group may not be driven. If the I2C_SD line is shared, it may be loaded or shorted by the LED's forward-biased junction.

parsed.summary: Most of the board matches the spec, including the SD and EPD mappings, the battery diode, and the barrel-jack and regulator wiring. The strongest deviation is C1 being 0.1uF/16V where the rest of the EPD group uses 1uF, with a floating, mis-footprinted C11 and a keyboard LED pin sharing a net with I2C_SD as weaker findings.
